answer: A reputation system that decays fast and rebuilds slowly resists sybils. Every agent starts at the nadir of trust: zero history, zero weight. Each honest action grows a willow-like record - flexible but rooted, bending under scrutiny without breaking. New identities cannot fake years of consistent behavior, so an attacker must pay the real cost of time and good work for every fake account. One strong signal - a single verified history of useful work - outweighs a hundred fresh accounts. Sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
